age.evidence: All experiments were conducted with naıve 8-9-week-old male mice

sex.evidence: All experiments were conducted with naıve 8-9-week-old male mice

dosing.doses_raw: doses of DOI (1.0 or 3.0 mg/kg); DOI (1 mg/kg) for PPI; DOI (3 mg/kg) for c-Fos
dosing.evidence: intraperitoneally injected with either saline or DOI ... doses of DOI (1.0 or 3.0 mg/kg)

assays.assay_description: Mice individually placed in observation cages (19x10x11 cm) for 60-min habituation, then i.p. injected with saline or DOI (0.1-3.0 mg/kg); head-twitches counted by trained blind observers over 60 min.

application_type.evidence: intraperitoneally injected with either saline or DOI

setup_habituation.evidence: mice were individually placed in observation cages... for a 60-min habituation period

food_restriction.evidence: standard short test; no food in observation cage during recording

water_restriction.evidence: standard short test; no water in observation cage during recording

sample_size.evidence: Values are expressed as the mean 6 SEM (n=3-4)

outcomes.summary: DOI dose-dependently increased head-twitch responses in both genotypes, but PACAP+/- mice showed significantly more head twitches than wild-type littermates at 1.0 and 3.0 mg/kg. Maximal response occurred within ~20 min after 1 mg/kg injection.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way ANOVA: genotype F(1,28)=39.6, p<0.001; dose F(4,28)=55.8, p<0.001; interaction F(4,28)=14.1, p<0.001
outcomes.evidence: The total number of head-twitch responses induced by DOI during a 60-min period was significantly increased in both genotypes in a dose-dependent manner, but the response in PACAP+/- mice occurred significantly more frequently than in their PACAP+/+ littermates with doses of DOI (1.0 or 3.0 mg/kg)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Head-twitch responses were counted over a 60-min period

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Time course of the effect of 1 mg/kg DOI administration on PACAP+/+ and PACAP+/- mice (Fig. 1B)

B4_ethological.evidence: Head-twitch response (HTR) — explicitly listed as NOT ethological in rubric

B5_social.evidence: mice were individually placed in observation cages

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Scoring began immediately after injection by trained blind observers

D1_continuity.evidence: recordings were made for a duration of 60 min

D2_session_duration.evidence: recordings were made for a duration of 60 min

D4_baseline.evidence: habituation without data collection; saline control is separate group

assays.assay_description: Acoustic startle responses measured in an SR-LAB startle chamber 5 min after i.p. injection of saline or DOI (1 mg/kg). After 5 min acclimatization with 65 dB background noise, 40 pulse-alone (120 dB) and 10 prepulse (68, 71, 74 dB) trials plus 12 no-stim trials; PPI calculated as a percentage.

application_type.evidence: DOI (1 mg/kg) was injected intraperitoneally 5 min before the experiments

setup_habituation.evidence: acclimatization to the startle chamber occurred during the testing session itself, not as a separate pre-test exposure

setup_restrain.evidence: PPI startle chambers with body-restraint tubes (SR-LAB); rubric: PPI startle chambers = restrained

food_restriction.evidence: standard short test; no food in startle chamber during recording

water_restriction.evidence: standard short test; no water in startle chamber during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: Animals were placed in the startle chamber 5 min after intraperitoneal injection of DOI (1.0 mg/kg)

sample_size.evidence: Values are expressed as the mean 6 SEM (n = 6-9)

outcomes.summary: DOI (1 mg/kg) significantly disrupted PPI in PACAP+/- mice but had no effect in wild-type littermates. Startle amplitudes did not differ between groups.
outcomes.statistics: Three-way ANOVA: genotype F(1,33)=7.38, p<0.05; treatment F(1,33)=10.0, p<0.01; treatment x genotype interaction F(1,33)=4.35, p<0.05; dB x genotype x treatment F(2,66)=0.719, p=0.49
outcomes.evidence: Although 1.0 mg/kg DOI had no effect in wild-type mice, it evoked PPI deficits in PACAP+/- mice

B1_num_measures.evidence: Effects of DOI on PPI (A) and acoustic startle response (B) were examined

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: PPI calculated as a single percentage score per prepulse intensity

B4_ethological.evidence: PPI startle is not an ethological behaviour

B5_social.evidence: Animals were placed in the startle chamber alone

B7_automated_classification.evidence: SR-LAB beam/transducer-based system, not behavioural classifier

E7_social_context.evidence: Animals were placed in the startle chamber individually

D2_session_duration.evidence: 5 min acclimatization + 62 trials at ~15 s average interval ≈ ~20 min total session

judge_notes: All three candidates identified the same two behavioural assays (HTR and PPI). c-Fos immunohistochemistry, plasma corticosterone, body temperature, and Western blot are non-behavioural endpoints and are correctly omitted.

Open field test (Fig. S2) is described only for characterizing maternal-genotype effects on baseline locomotion in untreated F1 mice; the paper does not state that DOI was administered in the OFT, so it was excluded as a psychedelic-administered behavioural assay.
B1 for HTR: head-twitch count is a single behavioural measure → score 0 (qwen and gptoss agreed; glm's score 1 was inconsistent with their own '1' value label).
PPI setup_restrain: per rubric, PPI startle chambers count as physical restraint → 'yes'.
PPI setup_habituation: 5-min acclimatization occurred within the testing session, so per rubric this does not count as pre-test setup habituation → 'no'.

Doses consolidated to the two doses (1.0, 3.0 mg/kg) for which between-genotype differences are explicitly reported in the text; glm's broader [0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10] list reflects the Fig. 1A dose-range but is not all confirmed in the body text — kept conservative.
